newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines may negotiate over steel firm.
newsitem.headline: Philippines may negotiate over steel firm.

text.p: The Philippines' National Steel Corp (NSC) said on Wednesday it may open negotiations with companies which had earlier expressed interest in acquiring a 20 percent stake in the company.
An attempt to auction off the 20 percent stake failed on Wednesday with no bids being submitted.

"We (may) negotiate with interested parties ... but we cannot go lower than nine pesos per share because that's the effective purchase price by Wing Tiek," Arthur Aguilar, general manager of the National Development Co (NDC), told Reuters.
The state NDC controls the government's remaining 25 percent stake in the steel firm.

Aguilar said if the talks failed, the government could then offer the shares to Malaysia's Wing Tiek Holdings Bhd which, along with its partner Marubeni Corp, recently acquired 75 percent of the formerly state-owned company.
Another option was that the government may decide to retain the stake, he said.
The government had offered 20 percent of its remaining stake for a minimum price of 10 pesos per share.
Twelve companies had earlier expressed interest but none offered bids at the auction.
Among companies which had attended a pre-bidding conference were Tomen Corp, Mitsui & Co Ltd, Kawasho Corp, Marubeni Corp, Urban Bank, and APC Group Inc.
Aguilar said the auction probably failed because the investment involved was too high for what would be a minority stake in the company.
The 20 percent stake, equivalent to over 448 million shares, would mean a price of over 4.4 billion pesos at the government's 10 peso per share level.
The government wants to sell the remaining five percent to small shareholders at a later date.
